62:   wifi.sta_mode = WAPI_MODE_MANAGED;
63:   if (!network->config.sta_open_network &&
64:       network->config.sta_password[0] != '\0')
65:     {

94: static int vs_network_apply_ap(struct vs_network_s *network)

97:   struct in_addr address;
98:   struct in_addr netmask;
99:   struct velasight_prov_config_s provision;
100:   int ret;
101: 
102:   if (network->config.ap_channel < 1 || network->config.ap_channel > 14 ||
103:       network->config.ap_ssid[0] == '\0')
104:     return -EINVAL;
105: 
106:   ret = wapi_set_ifdown(network->sock, "wlan0");
107:   if (ret < 0 && ret != -ENODEV)
108:     return ret;
109: 
110:   ret = wapi_set_ifup(network->sock, "wlan0");

112:     return ret;
113: 
114:   memset(&wifi, 0, sizeof(wifi));
115:   wifi.ifname = "wlan0";
116:   wifi.sta_mode = WAPI_MODE_MASTER;
117:   if (network->config.ap_password[0] != '\0')
118:     {
119:       wifi.auth_wpa = WPA_VER_2;
120:       wifi.cipher_mode = IW_AUTH_CIPHER_CCMP;
121:       wifi.alg = WPA_ALG_CCMP;
122:     }
123:   wifi.freq = network->config.ap_channel;

125:   wifi.ssid = network->config.ap_ssid;
126:   wifi.ssidlen = strlen(wifi.ssid);
127:   wifi.passphrase = network->config.ap_password;
128:   wifi.phraselen = strlen(wifi.passphrase);
129: 
130:   ret = wpa_driver_wext_associate(&wifi);
131:   if (ret < 0)
132:     goto fail;
133: 
134:   address.s_addr = htonl(0xc0a80a01);
135:   netmask.s_addr = htonl(0xffffff00);
136:   ret = netlib_set_ipv4addr("wlan0", &address);

146:     goto fail;
147: 
148:   network->dhcp_running = true;
149:   memset(&provision, 0, sizeof(provision));
150:   provision.one_shot = true;
151:   provision.on_saved = vs_network_provision_saved;
152:   provision.cb_arg = network;
153:   ret = velasight_provisioning_start(&provision);
154:   if (ret < 0)
155:     goto fail;
156: 
157:   network->mode = VS_NET_AP;
158:   network->status.mode = VS_NET_AP;
159:   network->status.state = VS_NET_AP_READY;
160:   snprintf(network->status.ssid, sizeof(network->status.ssid), "%s",
161:            network->config.ap_ssid);
162:   snprintf(network->status.password, sizeof(network->status.password), "%s",
163:            network->config.ap_password);
164:   snprintf(network->status.address, sizeof(network->status.address),
165:            "192.168.1.1");
166:   return 0;
167: 
168: fail:
169:   (void)velasight_provisioning_stop();
170:   if (network->dhcp_running)
171:     {
172:       (void)dhcpd_stop();
173:       network->dhcp_running = false;
174:     }

179: int vs_network_open(struct vs_network_s **network)
180: {
181:   struct vs_network_s *n;
182:   int ret;
183: 
184:   if (network == NULL)
185:     return -EINVAL;
186: 
187:   n = calloc(1, sizeof(*n));
188:   if (n == NULL)
189:     return -ENOMEM;
190: 
191:   ret = pthread_mutex_init(&n->event_lock, NULL);
192:   if (ret != 0)
193:     {
194:       free(n);
195:       return -ret;
196:     }
197: 
198:   n->sock = wapi_make_socket();
199:   if (n->sock < 0)
200:     {
201:       ret = n->sock;
202:       pthread_mutex_destroy(&n->event_lock);
203:       free(n);
204:       return ret;
205:     }
206: 
207:   ret = vs_config_load_wifi(&n->config);
208:   if (ret < 0)
209:     {
210:       close(n->sock);
211:       pthread_mutex_destroy(&n->event_lock);
212:       free(n);
213:       return ret;
214:     }
215: 
216:   n->mode = VS_NET_STA;
217:   n->status.mode = VS_NET_STA;
218:   n->status.state = VS_NET_DOWN;
219:   *network = n;
220:   return 0;
221: }

223: int vs_network_request_mode(struct vs_network_s *network,
224:                             enum vs_net_mode_e mode)
225: {
226:   int ret;
227: 
228:   if (network == NULL)
229:     return -EINVAL;
230: 
231:   network->status.state = VS_NET_SWITCHING;
232: 
233:   if (network->mode == VS_NET_AP && mode == VS_NET_STA)
234:     {
235:       ret = velasight_provisioning_stop();
236:       if (ret < 0 && ret != -EALREADY)
237:         {
238:           network->status.state = VS_NET_ERROR;
239:           network->status.error = ret;
240:           return ret;
241:         }
242:     }
243: 
244:   if (network->dhcp_running)
245:     {
246:       (void)dhcpd_stop();
247:       network->dhcp_running = false;
248:     }
249: 
250:   ret = mode == VS_NET_AP ? vs_network_apply_ap(network) :
251:                              vs_network_apply_sta(network);
252:   if (ret < 0)
253:     {
254:       network->status.state = VS_NET_ERROR;
255:       network->status.error = ret;
256:     }
257: 
258:   return ret;
259: }

262: {

266: 
267:   if (network == NULL)
268:     return 0;

271:   if (!network->provision_event)
272:     {
273:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&network->event_lock);
274:       return 0;
275:     }
276: 
277:   network->provision_event = false;
278:   status = network->provision_status;
279:   pthread_mutex_unlock(&network->event_lock);
280:   if (status < 0)
281:     {
282:       network->status.error = status;
283:       network->status.state = VS_NET_ERROR;
284:       return status;
285:     }
286: 
287:   ret = vs_config_load_wifi(&config);
288:   if (ret < 0)
289:     {
290:       network->status.error = ret;
291:       network->status.state = VS_NET_ERROR;
292:       return ret;
293:     }
294: 
295:   network->config = config;
296:   ret = vs_network_request_mode(network, VS_NET_STA);
297:   return ret < 0 ? ret : 1;
298: }

169:   if (event->type == VS_INPUT_PROGRESS && event->key == VS_KEY_BACK &&
170:       (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_RUNNING ||
171:        runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_PAUSED ||
172:        runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_EXITING))
173:     {
174:       if (runtime->page != VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_EXITING)
175:         {
176:           runtime->social_exit_from_paused =
177:             runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_PAUSED;
178:         }
179: 
180:       runtime->page = VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_EXITING;
181:       runtime->progress = event->progress;
182:       return;
183:     }
184: 
185:   if (event->type == VS_INPUT_PROGRESS && event->key == VS_KEY_BACK &&
186:        (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOFTAP ||
187:         (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_NET_SWITCHING &&
188:          runtime->network.mode == VS_NET_AP) ||
189:         runtime->page == VS_PAGE_ERROR))
190:     {
191:       if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_ERROR)
192:         {
193:           runtime->error_back_progress = true;
194:         }
195:       else
196:         {
197:           runtime->page = VS_PAGE_NET_SWITCHING;
198:         }
199: 
200:       runtime->progress = event->progress;
201:       return;
202:     }
203: 
204:   if (event->type == VS_INPUT_CANCEL && event->key == VS_KEY_CONFIRM &&
205:       runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_ENTER)
206:     {
207:       runtime->page = VS_PAGE_HISTORY;
208:       runtime->progress = 0;
209:       return;
210:     }
211: 
212:   if (event->type == VS_INPUT_CANCEL && event->key == VS_KEY_BACK &&
213:       (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_NET_SWITCHING ||
214:        runtime->page == VS_PAGE_ERROR))
215:     {
216:       if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_NET_SWITCHING)
217:         {
218:           runtime->page = VS_PAGE_SOFTAP;
219:         }
220: 
221:       runtime->progress = 0;
222:       runtime->error_back_progress = false;
223:       return;
224:     }
225: 
226:   if (event->type == VS_INPUT_NET_TOGGLE &&
227:       (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_HISTORY ||
228:        runtime->page == VS_PAGE_NET_SWITCHING) &&
229:       network != NULL)
230:     {
231:       vs_switch_network(display, runtime, network);
232:       return;
233:     }
234: 
235:   if (event->type == VS_INPUT_SHORT)
236:     {
237:       if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_HISTORY)
238:         {
239:           if (event->key == VS_KEY_CONFIRM)
240:             {
241:               /* Keep a visible assistant entry page until the voice backend
242:                * is connected in the next implementation phase. */
243:               runtime->page = VS_PAGE_VOICE_LISTENING;
244:             }
245:           else if (event->key == VS_KEY_BACK)
246:             runtime->page = VS_PAGE_HISTORY;
247:           else if (event->key == VS_KEY_NEXT)
248:             {
249:               runtime->index = (runtime->index + 1) %
250:                                (sizeof(g_history) / sizeof(g_history[0]));
251:               runtime->view = VS_HISTORY_SUMMARY;
252:             }
253:         }
254:       else if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_RUNNING &&
255:                event->key == VS_KEY_CONFIRM)
256:         {
257:           runtime->page = VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_PAUSED;
258:         }
259:       else if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_PAUSED &&
260:                event->key == VS_KEY_CONFIRM)
261:         {
262:           runtime->page = VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_RUNNING;
263:         }
264:       else if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_VOICE_LISTENING &&
265:                event->key == VS_KEY_CONFIRM)
266:         {
267:           runtime->page = VS_PAGE_VOICE_THINKING;
268:         }
269:       else if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_ENTER &&
270:                event->key == VS_KEY_CONFIRM)
271:         {
272:           runtime->page = VS_PAGE_VOICE_LISTENING;
273:           runtime->progress = 0;
274:         }
275:       else if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_EXITING &&
276:                event->key == VS_KEY_BACK)
277:         {
278:           runtime->page = runtime->social_exit_from_paused ?
279:                           VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_PAUSED : VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_RUNNING;
280:           runtime->progress = 0;
281:         }
282:       else if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_NET_SWITCHING &&
283:                runtime->network.mode == VS_NET_AP &&
284:                event->key == VS_KEY_BACK)
285:         {
286:           runtime->page = VS_PAGE_SOFTAP;
287:           runtime->progress = 0;
288:         }
289:       else if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_VOICE_SPEAKING)
290:         {
291:           runtime->page = VS_PAGE_HISTORY;
292:         }
293:       else if (event->key == VS_KEY_BACK &&
294:                runtime->page != VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_RUNNING &&
295:                runtime->page != VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_PAUSED &&
296:                runtime->page != VS_PAGE_SOFTAP &&
297:                runtime->page != VS_PAGE_NET_SWITCHING)
298:         {
299:           runtime->page = VS_PAGE_HISTORY;
300:           runtime->progress = 0;
301:           runtime->error_back_progress = false;
302:         }
303:     }
304:   else if (event->type == VS_INPUT_LONG)
305:     {
306:       if ((runtime->page == VS_PAGE_HISTORY ||
307:            runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_ENTER) &&
308:           event->key == VS_KEY_CONFIRM)
309:         {
310:           runtime->progress = 100;
311:           runtime->page = VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_RUNNING;
312:         }
313:       else if ((runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_RUNNING ||
314:                 runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_PAUSED ||
315:                 runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOCIAL_EXITING) &&
316:                event->key == VS_KEY_BACK)
317:         {
318:           runtime->page = VS_PAGE_HISTORY;
319:         }
320:       else if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOFTAP &&
321:                event->key == VS_KEY_CONFIRM)
322:         {
323:           /* Credential reset belongs to the future SoftAP service. */
324:           runtime->page = VS_PAGE_SOFTAP;
325:         }
326:       else if ((runtime->page == VS_PAGE_SOFTAP ||
327:                 (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_NET_SWITCHING &&
328:                  runtime->network.mode == VS_NET_AP)) &&
329:                event->key == VS_KEY_BACK && network != NULL)
330:         {
331:           vs_switch_network(display, runtime, network);
332:         }
333:       else if (runtime->page == VS_PAGE_ERROR && event->key == VS_KEY_BACK)
334:         {
335:           if (network != NULL && runtime->network.mode == VS_NET_AP)
336:             {
337:               (void)vs_network_request_mode(network, VS_NET_STA);
338:               (void)vs_network_get_status(network, &runtime->network);
339:             }
340: 
341:           runtime->page = VS_PAGE_HISTORY;
342:           runtime->progress = 0;
343:           runtime->error_back_progress = false;
344:         }
345:     }
346: }
347: 
348: int vs_app_run(void)
349: {
350:   struct vs_display_s *display = NULL;
351:   struct vs_input_s *input = NULL;
352:   struct vs_network_s *network = NULL;
353:   struct vs_runtime_s runtime;
354:   struct vs_input_event_s event;
355:   int ret;
356: 
357:   memset(&runtime, 0, sizeof(runtime));
358:   runtime.page = VS_PAGE_HISTORY;
359:   runtime.view = VS_HISTORY_SUMMARY;
360:   runtime.network.mode = VS_NET_STA;
361:   runtime.network.state = VS_NET_DOWN;
362: 
363:   ret = vs_display_open(&display);
364:   if (ret < 0)
365:     return ret;
366:   ret = vs_input_open(&input);
367:   if (ret < 0)
368:     goto fail;
369:   ret = vs_network_open(&network);
370:   if (ret < 0)
371:     {
372:       runtime.network.state = VS_NET_ERROR;
373:       runtime.network.error = ret;
374:     }
375:   else if (vs_network_request_mode(network, VS_NET_STA) < 0)
376:     {
377:       (void)vs_network_get_status(network, &runtime.network);
378:       runtime.error = runtime.network.error;
379:       runtime.page = VS_PAGE_ERROR;
380:     }
381: 
382:   runtime.agent = velaclaw_client_open("velasight");
383:   if (runtime.agent == NULL)
384:     {
385:       printf("velasight: ai_agent client unavailable\n");
386:     }
387: 
388:   vs_render(display, &runtime);
389:   for (;;)
390:     {
391:       if (network != NULL)
392:         {
393:           ret = vs_network_process_events(network);
394:           if (ret != 0)
395:             {
396:               (void)vs_network_get_status(network, &runtime.network);
397:               if (ret < 0)
398:                 {
399:                   runtime.error = ret;
400:                   runtime.page = VS_PAGE_ERROR;
401:                 }
402:               else
403:                 {
404:                   runtime.page = VS_PAGE_HISTORY;
405:                 }
406: 
407:               vs_render(display, &runtime);
408:             }
409:         }
410: 
411:       if (vs_input_poll(input, &event) > 0)
412:         {
413:           enum vs_page_e previous = runtime.page;
414: 
415:           vs_handle_event(display, &runtime, network, &event);
416:           if (runtime.page != previous || event.type == VS_INPUT_LONG ||
417:               event.type == VS_INPUT_CANCEL)
418:             {
419:               printf("velasight: input type=%u key=%u progress=%u "
420:                      "page=%u->%u\n", event.type, event.key,
421:                      event.progress, previous, runtime.page);
422:             }
423: 
424:           vs_render(display, &runtime);
425:         }
426:       vs_display_tick(display);
427:       usleep(CONFIG_VS_INPUT_POLL_MS * 1000);
428:     }
429: 
430: fail:
431:   vs_network_close(network);
432:   vs_input_close(input);
433:   vs_display_close(display);
434:   return ret;
435: }

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * app/provisioning_web/include/velasight_provisioning.h
3:  *
4:  * AP-mode provisioning web entry.  The application switches the radio into
5:  * SoftAP itself, calls velasight_provisioning_start(), and gets told when a
6:  * phone has submitted credentials.  This service never touches the Wi-Fi
7:  * role: it does not associate, does not run wapi, does not start DHCPD and
8:  * does not switch back to STA.  Owning both the HTTP page and the radio would
9:  * make it impossible for the application to decide when the network may drop.
10:  *
11:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
12:  ****************************************************************************/
13: 
14: #ifndef __APP_PROVISIONING_WEB_INCLUDE_VELASIGHT_PROVISIONING_H
15: #define __APP_PROVISIONING_WEB_INCLUDE_VELASIGHT_PROVISIONING_H
16: 
17: #include <stdbool.h>
18: #include <stddef.h>
19: #include <stdint.h>
20: 
21: #ifdef __cplusplus
22: extern "C"
23: {
24: #endif
25: 
26: /* IEEE 802.11 SSID length, and the WPA2 passphrase range.  An empty password
27:  * means an open network, which is the only reason 0 is legal.
28:  */
29: 
30: #define VELASIGHT_PROV_SSID_MAX 32
31: #define VELASIGHT_PROV_PSK_MIN  8
32: #define VELASIGHT_PROV_PSK_MAX  63
33: 
34: /* Where the record lives when the caller passes no path.  On SD-NAND, so it
35:  * survives a reset; /mnt itself is pseudo-filesystem and /mnt/ram is a PSRAM
36:  * ramdisk, neither of which would.
37:  *
38:  * Every component fits 8.3 because that SD-NAND is VFAT without long-name
39:  * support (CONFIG_FAT_LFN is not set): a "velasight" directory or a
40:  * "wifi-provision.bin" file is rejected outright with -EINVAL.
41:  */
42: 
43: #ifndef CONFIG_VELASIGHT_PROVISION_STORE
44: #  define CONFIG_VELASIGHT_PROVISION_STORE "/mnt/sdnand/prov/wifi.bin"
45: #endif
46: 
47: #ifndef CONFIG_VELASIGHT_PROVISION_PORT
48: #  define CONFIG_VELASIGHT_PROVISION_PORT 80
49: #endif
50: 
51: struct velasight_prov_credentials_s
52: {
53:   char     ssid[VELASIGHT_PROV_SSID_MAX + 1];
54:   char     password[VELASIGHT_PROV_PSK_MAX + 1];
55:   uint32_t generation;   /* Monotonic save counter, first save is 1 */
56:   bool     open_network; /* Password is empty */
57: };
58: 
59: /* Called after the success page has been written and the connection closed,
60:  * never before: the application is expected to leave SoftAP from here, and
61:  * doing that mid-response is what makes a phone show "submit failed" for a
62:  * save that actually happened.
63:  *
64:  * status is 0 on success or a negative errno.  Credentials are deliberately
65:  * absent -- read them with velasight_provisioning_load() so a passphrase does
66:  * not travel through every callback that only wanted the notification.
67:  */
68: 
69: typedef void (*velasight_prov_saved_cb_t)(int status, uint32_t generation,
70:                                           void *arg);
71: 
72: struct velasight_prov_config_s
73: {
74:   uint16_t                  port;       /* 0 selects the built-in default */
75:   bool                      one_shot;   /* Stop after one accepted submit */
76:   const char               *store_path; /* NULL selects the built-in path */
77:   velasight_prov_saved_cb_t on_saved;   /* May be NULL */
78:   void                     *cb_arg;
79: };
80: 
81: /****************************************************************************
82:  * Name: velasight_provisioning_start
83:  *
84:  * Description:
85:  *   Bind the HTTP port and start the listener thread.  Returns 0, -EALREADY
86:  *   if it is already running, or a negative errno.  A NULL config means all
87:  *   defaults.  The config is copied, so the caller may free it.
88:  *
89:  ****************************************************************************/
90: 
91: int velasight_provisioning_start(
92:     const struct velasight_prov_config_s *config);
93: 
94: /****************************************************************************
95:  * Name: velasight_provisioning_stop
96:  *
97:  * Description:
98:  *   Close the listener and join the thread.  Returns 0, or -EALREADY when
99:  *   nothing was running.  Safe to call from the saved callback.
100:  *
101:  ****************************************************************************/
102: 
103: int velasight_provisioning_stop(void);
104: 
105: bool velasight_provisioning_is_running(void);
106: 
107: /* Saves observed in this process; 0 before the first one.  Persisted saves
108:  * from earlier boots are counted by the generation inside the record.
109:  */
110: 
111: uint32_t velasight_provisioning_generation(void);
112: 
113: /****************************************************************************
114:  * Name: velasight_provisioning_load
115:  *
116:  * Description:
117:  *   Read the stored credentials.  Returns 0, -ENOENT when nothing has been
118:  *   provisioned, -EBADMSG when the record is corrupt, or a negative errno.
119:  *
120:  ****************************************************************************/
121: 
122: int velasight_provisioning_load(
123:     struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *out);
124: 
125: int velasight_provisioning_load_from(
126:     const char *path, struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *out);
127: 
128: #ifdef __cplusplus
129: }
130: #endif
131: 
132: #endif /* __APP_PROVISIONING_WEB_INCLUDE_VELASIGHT_PROVISIONING_H */

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * app/provisioning_web/vp_server.c
3:  *
4:  * The socket half of the provisioning entry.  Deliberately POSIX-only so the
5:  * accept loop, the ordering guarantee and one-shot mode can be exercised over
6:  * loopback on the host; the only thing left for the board is whether the
7:  * SoftAP and SD-NAND are actually there.
8:  *
9:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
10:  ****************************************************************************/
11: 
12: #include <arpa/inet.h>
13: #include <errno.h>
14: #include <netinet/in.h>
15: #include <poll.h>
16: #include <pthread.h>
17: #include <stdbool.h>
18: #include <stdio.h>
19: #include <string.h>
20: #include <sys/socket.h>
21: #include <unistd.h>
22: 
23: #include "velasight_provisioning.h"
24: #include "vp_form.h"
25: #include "vp_http.h"
26: #include "vp_store.h"
27: 
28: #define VP_STATE_IDLE     0
29: #define VP_STATE_RUNNING  1
30: #define VP_STATE_FINISHED 2  /* the thread returned, still needs a join */
31: 
32: #define VP_ACCEPT_POLL_MS  200
33: #define VP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS 5000
34: #define VP_STORE_PATH_MAX  192
35: #define VP_THREAD_STACK    8192
36: 
37: struct vp_server_s
38: {
39:   int       listenfd;
40:   pthread_t thread;
41:   int       state;
42:   bool      stopping;
43:   bool      one_shot;
44:   char      store_path[VP_STORE_PATH_MAX];
45:   uint32_t  generation;
46:   velasight_prov_saved_cb_t on_saved;
47:   void     *cb_arg;
48: };
49: 
50: static struct vp_server_s g_server =
51: {
52:   .listenfd = -1,
53:   .state    = VP_STATE_IDLE,
54: };
55: 
56: static pthread_mutex_t g_lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
57: 
58: /* Request and response buffers are static because only one connection is
59:  * served at a time and 6KB of thread stack on this part is not free.
60:  */
61: 
62: static char g_request[VP_HTTP_MAX_HEADERS + VP_HTTP_MAX_BODY + 1];
63: static char g_response[VP_HTTP_RESPONSE_MAX];
64: 
65: static int vp_write_all(int fd, const char *data, size_t len)
66: {
67:   size_t sent = 0;
68: 
69:   while (sent < len)
70:     {
71:       ssize_t n = write(fd, data + sent, len - sent);
72: 
73:       if (n < 0)
74:         {
75:           if (errno == EINTR)
76:             {
77:               continue;
78:             }
79: 
80:           return -errno;
81:         }
82: 
83:       if (n == 0)
84:         {
85:           return -EPIPE;
86:         }
87: 
88:       sent += (size_t)n;
89:     }
90: 
91:   return 0;
92: }
93: 
94: /****************************************************************************
95:  * Name: vp_read_request
96:  *
97:  * Description:
98:  *   Read until the headers plus the declared body have arrived, the cap is
99:  *   reached or the deadline passes.  Returns the total length, or negative on
100:  *   error.  A client that opens a connection and says nothing costs one
101:  *   timeout, not the service.
102:  *
103:  ****************************************************************************/
104: 
105: static int vp_read_request(int fd, struct vp_http_request_s *req)
106: {
107:   size_t total = 0;
108:   int waited = 0;
109: 
110:   for (; ; )
111:     {
112:       struct pollfd pfd;
113:       ssize_t n;
114:       int ret;
115: 
116:       ret = vp_http_parse(g_request, total, req);
117:       if (ret == 0)
118:         {
119:           if (req->action != VP_HTTP_ACTION_SAVE ||
120:               total >= req->header_len + req->content_length)
121:             {
122:               return (int)total;
123:             }
124:         }
125:       else if (ret != -EAGAIN)
126:         {
127:           return ret;
128:         }
129: 
130:       if (total >= sizeof(g_request) - 1)
131:         {
132:           return -E2BIG;
133:         }
134: 
135:       pfd.fd = fd;
136:       pfd.events = POLLIN;
137:       pfd.revents = 0;
138:       ret = poll(&pfd, 1, VP_ACCEPT_POLL_MS);
139:       if (ret < 0)
140:         {
141:           if (errno == EINTR)
142:             {
143:               continue;
144:             }
145: 
146:           return -errno;
147:         }
148: 
149:       if (ret == 0)
150:         {
151:           waited += VP_ACCEPT_POLL_MS;
152:           if (waited >= VP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS)
153:             {
154:               return -ETIMEDOUT;
155:             }
156: 
157:           continue;
158:         }
159: 
160:       n = read(fd, g_request + total, sizeof(g_request) - 1 - total);
161:       if (n < 0)
162:         {
163:           if (errno == EINTR)
164:             {
165:               continue;
166:             }
167: 
168:           return -errno;
169:         }
170: 
171:       if (n == 0)
172:         {
173:           /* Peer closed.  Whatever arrived is all there will be, so let the
174:            * parser decide between "incomplete" and "answerable".
175:            */
176: 
177:           if (vp_http_parse(g_request, total, req) == 0 &&
178:               (req->action != VP_HTTP_ACTION_SAVE ||
179:                total >= req->header_len + req->content_length))
180:             {
181:               return (int)total;
182:             }
183: 
184:           return -ECONNRESET;
185:         }
186: 
187:       total += (size_t)n;
188:     }
189: }
190: 
191: /****************************************************************************
192:  * Name: vp_handle
193:  *
194:  * Description:
195:  *   Serve one connection.  Sets *saved when credentials were persisted and
196:  *   *save_status to 0 or the negative errno of a failed save, so the caller can
197:  *   notify the application only after the socket is gone.
198:  *
199:  ****************************************************************************/
200: 
201: static void vp_handle(int fd, bool *saved, int *save_status,
202:                       uint32_t *generation)
203: {
204:   struct velasight_prov_credentials_s cred;
205:   struct vp_http_request_s req;
206:   size_t len = 0;
207:   int ret;
208: 
209:   *saved = false;
210:   *save_status = 0;
211: 
212:   ret = vp_read_request(fd, &req);
213:   if (ret < 0)
214:     {
215:       if (ret == -E2BIG)
216:         {
217:           len = vp_http_status_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response), 431,
218:                                     "请求过大。");
219:         }
220:       else
221:         {
222:           /* Nothing usable arrived; answering a client that already gave up
223:            * is not worth a second syscall.
224:            */
225: 
226:           return;
227:         }
228:     }
229:   else if (req.action == VP_HTTP_ACTION_PAGE)
230:     {
231:       len = vp_http_form_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response), NULL);
232:     }
233:   else if (req.action == VP_HTTP_ACTION_REJECT)
234:     {
235:       len = vp_http_status_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response), req.status,
236:                                req.status == 404 ? "页面不存在。" :
237:                                req.status == 405 ? "不支持该请求方法。" :
238:                                req.status == 413 ? "提交内容过大。" :
239:                                req.status == 415 ? "提交格式不受支持。" :
240:                                req.status == 411 ? "缺少 Content-Length。" :
241:                                                    "请求无法解析。");
242:     }
243:   else
244:     {
245:       memset(&cred, 0, sizeof(cred));
246:       ret = vp_form_parse(g_request + req.header_len, req.content_length,
247:                           &cred);
248:       if (ret < 0)
249:         {
250:           /* No detail about which field failed and no echo of what was typed:
251:            * the notice has to be useful to the person at the phone without

298: static void *vp_thread(void *arg)
299: {
300:   (void)arg;
301: 
302:   for (; ; )
303:     {
304:       struct pollfd pfd;
305:       uint32_t generation = 0;
306:       int save_status = 0;
307:       bool saved = false;
308:       bool stopping;
309:       int fd;
310:       int ret;
311: 
312:       pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
313:       stopping = g_server.stopping;
314:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
315:       if (stopping)
316:         {
317:           break;
318:         }
319: 
320:       pfd.fd = g_server.listenfd;
321:       pfd.events = POLLIN;
322:       pfd.revents = 0;
323: 
324:       /* Polling rather than blocking in accept(): stop() then needs no signal
325:        * and no socket shutdown trick that may or may not wake accept on a
326:        * given stack.
327:        *
328:        * This requires CONFIG_NET_TCPBACKLOG on NuttX, which the Kconfig
329:        * depends on.  Without it TCP_BACKLOG events never fire, POLLIN on a
330:        * listening socket is unreachable, and accept() blocks with no timeout
331:        * at all -- measured on the board as a service that reported
332:        * "listening" and then answered nothing.
333:        */
334: 
335:       ret = poll(&pfd, 1, VP_ACCEPT_POLL_MS);
336:       if (ret < 0)
337:         {
338:           if (errno == EINTR)
339:             {
340:               continue;
341:             }
342: 
343:           break;
344:         }
345: 
346:       if (ret == 0)
347:         {
348:           continue;
349:         }
350: 
351:       fd = accept(g_server.listenfd, NULL, NULL);
352:       if (fd < 0)
353:         {
354:           if (errno == EINTR || errno == ECONNABORTED)
355:             {
356:               continue;
357:             }
358: 
359:           break;
360:         }
361: 
362:       vp_handle(fd, &saved, &save_status, &generation);
363: 
364:       /* Close before notifying.  The application is expected to leave SoftAP
365:        * from the callback, and doing that with the response still in flight is
366:        * what makes a successful save look like a failed submit on the phone.
367:        */
368: 
369:       shutdown(fd, SHUT_RDWR);
370:       close(fd);
371: 
372:       if (saved)
373:         {
374:           pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
375:           g_server.generation = generation;
376:           pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
377:         }
378: 
379:       if (saved || save_status < 0)
380:         {
381:           if (g_server.on_saved != NULL)
382:             {
383:               g_server.on_saved(save_status, generation, g_server.cb_arg);
384:             }
385:         }
386: 
387:       if (saved && g_server.one_shot)
388:         {
389:           break;
390:         }
391: 
392:       pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
393:       stopping = g_server.stopping;
394:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
395:       if (stopping)
396:         {
397:           break;
398:         }
399:     }
400: 
401:   pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
402:   if (g_server.listenfd >= 0)
403:     {
404:       close(g_server.listenfd);
405:       g_server.listenfd = -1;
406:     }
407: 
408:   g_server.state = VP_STATE_FINISHED;
409:   pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
410:   return NULL;
411: }

415: static void vp_reap_locked(void)
416: {
417:   if (g_server.state == VP_STATE_FINISHED)
418:     {
419:       pthread_t thread = g_server.thread;
420: 
421:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
422:       pthread_join(thread, NULL);
423:       pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
424:       g_server.state = VP_STATE_IDLE;

428: int velasight_provisioning_start(
429:     const struct velasight_prov_config_s *config)
430: {
431:   struct velasight_prov_config_s cfg;
432:   struct sockaddr_in addr;
433:   pthread_attr_t attr;
434:   uint16_t port;
435:   int one = 1;
436:   int fd;
437:   int ret;
438: 
439:   memset(&cfg, 0, sizeof(cfg));
440:   if (config != NULL)
441:     {
442:       cfg = *config;
443:     }
444: 
445:   if (cfg.store_path != NULL &&
446:       strlen(cfg.store_path) >= VP_STORE_PATH_MAX)
447:     {
448:       return -ENAMETOOLONG;
449:     }
450: 
451:   pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
452:   vp_reap_locked();
453:   if (g_server.state != VP_STATE_IDLE)
454:     {
455:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
456:       return -EALREADY;
457:     }
458: 
459:   port = cfg.port != 0 ? cfg.port :
460:          (uint16_t)CONFIG_VELASIGHT_PROVISION_PORT;
461: 
462:   fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
463:   if (fd < 0)
464:     {
465:       ret = -errno;
466:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
467:       return ret;
468:     }
469: 
470:   setsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, &one, sizeof(one));
471: 
472:   memset(&addr, 0, sizeof(addr));
473:   addr.sin_family      = AF_INET;
474:   addr.sin_port        = htons(port);
475:   addr.sin_addr.s_addr = htonl(INADDR_ANY);
476: 
477:   if (bind(fd, (struct sockaddr *)&addr, sizeof(addr)) < 0 ||
478:       listen(fd, 2) < 0)
479:     {
480:       ret = -errno;
481:       close(fd);
482:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
483:       return ret;
484:     }
485: 
486:   g_server.listenfd   = fd;
487:   g_server.stopping   = false;
488:   g_server.one_shot   = cfg.one_shot;
489:   g_server.generation = 0;
490:   g_server.on_saved   = cfg.on_saved;
491:   g_server.cb_arg     = cfg.cb_arg;
492:   snprintf(g_server.store_path, sizeof(g_server.store_path), "%s",
493:            cfg.store_path != NULL ? cfg.store_path :
494:            CONFIG_VELASIGHT_PROVISION_STORE);
495: 
496:   pthread_attr_init(&attr);
497:   pthread_attr_setstacksize(&attr, VP_THREAD_STACK);
498:   ret = pthread_create(&g_server.thread, &attr, vp_thread, NULL);
499:   pthread_attr_destroy(&attr);
500:   if (ret != 0)
501:     {
502:       close(fd);
503:       g_server.listenfd = -1;
504:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
505:       return -ret;
506:     }
507: 
508:   g_server.state = VP_STATE_RUNNING;
509:   pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
510: 
511:   printf("provision_web: listening on 0.0.0.0:%u, store %s\n",
512:          (unsigned)port, g_server.store_path);
513:   return 0;
514: }

516: int velasight_provisioning_stop(void)
517: {
518:   pthread_t thread;
519: 
520:   pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
521:   vp_reap_locked();
522:   if (g_server.state != VP_STATE_RUNNING)
523:     {
524:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
525:       return -EALREADY;
526:     }
527: 
528:   g_server.stopping = true;
529:   thread = g_server.thread;
530: 
531:   /* Called from the saved callback, which runs on the listener thread: joining
532:    * ourselves would deadlock, so only ask the loop to end and let the normal
533:    * exit path close the socket.  A later stop() from the application reaps it.
534:    */
535: 
536:   if (pthread_equal(thread, pthread_self()))
537:     {
538:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
539:       return 0;
540:     }
541: 
542:   pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
543:   pthread_join(thread, NULL);
544: 
545:   pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
546:   g_server.state = VP_STATE_IDLE;
547:   pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
548:   return 0;
549: }

557:   pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
558:   return running;

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * app/provisioning_web/vp_store.c
3:  *
4:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
5:  ****************************************************************************/
6: 
7: #include <errno.h>
8: #include <stdio.h>
9: #include <string.h>
10: #include <sys/stat.h>
11: #include <unistd.h>
12: 
13: #include "vp_form.h"
14: #include "vp_store.h"
15: 
16: #define VP_OFF_MAGIC     0
17: #define VP_OFF_VERSION   4
18: #define VP_OFF_FLAGS     6
19: #define VP_OFF_GEN       8
20: #define VP_OFF_SSID_LEN  12
21: #define VP_OFF_PSK_LEN   13
22: #define VP_OFF_SSID      14
23: #define VP_OFF_PSK       46
24: #define VP_OFF_RESERVED  109
25: #define VP_OFF_CRC       110
26: 
27: #define VP_STORE_PATH_MAX 192
28: 
29: uint32_t vp_crc32(const void *data, size_t len)
30: {
31:   const unsigned char *p = (const unsigned char *)data;
32:   uint32_t crc = 0xffffffffu;
33:   size_t i;
34: 
35:   /* Bitwise rather than a table: 114 bytes twice per save is not worth 1KB of
36:    * flash on a part that is already at 90% of its region.
37:    */
38: 
39:   for (i = 0; i < len; i++)
40:     {
41:       unsigned bit;
42: 
43:       crc ^= p[i];
44:       for (bit = 0; bit < 8; bit++)
45:         {
46:           crc = (crc >> 1) ^ (0xedb88320u & (uint32_t)(-(int32_t)(crc & 1u)));
47:         }
48:     }
49: 
50:   return crc ^ 0xffffffffu;
51: }
52: 
53: static void vp_put16(uint8_t *buf, uint16_t value)
54: {
55:   buf[0] = (uint8_t)(value & 0xffu);
56:   buf[1] = (uint8_t)((value >> 8) & 0xffu);
57: }
58: 
59: static void vp_put32(uint8_t *buf, uint32_t value)
60: {
61:   buf[0] = (uint8_t)(value & 0xffu);
62:   buf[1] = (uint8_t)((value >> 8) & 0xffu);
63:   buf[2] = (uint8_t)((value >> 16) & 0xffu);
64:   buf[3] = (uint8_t)((value >> 24) & 0xffu);
65: }
66: 
67: static uint16_t vp_get16(const uint8_t *buf)
68: {
69:   return (uint16_t)((uint16_t)buf[0] | (uint16_t)((uint16_t)buf[1] << 8));
70: }
71: 
72: static uint32_t vp_get32(const uint8_t *buf)
73: {
74:   return (uint32_t)buf[0] | ((uint32_t)buf[1] << 8) |
75:          ((uint32_t)buf[2] << 16) | ((uint32_t)buf[3] << 24);
76: }
77: 
78: static size_t vp_len(const char *s, size_t maxlen)
79: {
80:   size_t n = 0;
81: 
82:   while (n < maxlen && s[n] != '\0')
83:     {
84:       n++;
85:     }
86: 
87:   return n;
88: }
89: 
90: int vp_record_encode(uint8_t *buf, size_t buflen,
91:                      const struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred)
92: {
93:   size_t ssid_len;
94:   size_t psk_len;
95:   int ret;
96: 
97:   if (buf == NULL || cred == NULL)
98:     {
99:       return -EINVAL;
100:     }
101: 
102:   if (buflen < VP_RECORD_SIZE)
103:     {
104:       return -E2BIG;
105:     }
106: 
107:   ret = vp_credentials_validate(cred);
108:   if (ret < 0)
109:     {
110:       return ret;
111:     }
112: 
113:   ssid_len = vp_len(cred->ssid, sizeof(cred->ssid));
114:   psk_len  = vp_len(cred->password, sizeof(cred->password));
115: 
116:   memset(buf, 0, VP_RECORD_SIZE);
117:   memcpy(buf + VP_OFF_MAGIC, VP_RECORD_MAGIC, 4);
118:   vp_put16(buf + VP_OFF_VERSION, VP_RECORD_VERSION);
119:   vp_put16(buf + VP_OFF_FLAGS,
120:            cred->open_network ? VP_RECORD_FLAG_OPEN : 0);
121:   vp_put32(buf + VP_OFF_GEN, cred->generation);
122:   buf[VP_OFF_SSID_LEN] = (uint8_t)ssid_len;
123:   buf[VP_OFF_PSK_LEN]  = (uint8_t)psk_len;
124:   memcpy(buf + VP_OFF_SSID, cred->ssid, ssid_len);
125:   memcpy(buf + VP_OFF_PSK, cred->password, psk_len);
126:   vp_put32(buf + VP_OFF_CRC, vp_crc32(buf, VP_RECORD_SIZE - 4));
127:   return VP_RECORD_SIZE;
128: }
129: 
130: static bool vp_padding_is_zero(const uint8_t *buf, size_t offset,
131:                                size_t used, size_t field)
132: {
133:   size_t i;
134: 
135:   for (i = used; i < field; i++)
136:     {
137:       if (buf[offset + i] != 0)
138:         {
139:           return false;
140:         }
141:     }
142: 
143:   return true;
144: }
145: 
146: int vp_record_decode(const uint8_t *buf, size_t len,
147:                      struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred)
148: {
149:   struct velasight_prov_credentials_s parsed;
150:   size_t ssid_len;
151:   size_t psk_len;
152:   uint16_t flags;
153: 
154:   if (buf == NULL || cred == NULL)
155:     {
156:       return -EINVAL;
157:     }
158: 
159:   /* Exactly one size is legal.  A shorter file is a truncated write and a
160:    * longer one is not this format, and neither is worth guessing about.
161:    */
162: 
163:   if (len != VP_RECORD_SIZE)
164:     {
165:       return -EBADMSG;
166:     }
167: 
168:   if (memcmp(buf + VP_OFF_MAGIC, VP_RECORD_MAGIC, 4) != 0 ||
169:       vp_get16(buf + VP_OFF_VERSION) != VP_RECORD_VERSION ||
170:       buf[VP_OFF_RESERVED] != 0)
171:     {
172:       return -EBADMSG;
173:     }
174: 
175:   if (vp_get32(buf + VP_OFF_CRC) != vp_crc32(buf, VP_RECORD_SIZE - 4))
176:     {
177:       return -EBADMSG;
178:     }
179: 
180:   flags    = vp_get16(buf + VP_OFF_FLAGS);
181:   ssid_len = buf[VP_OFF_SSID_LEN];
182:   psk_len  = buf[VP_OFF_PSK_LEN];
183: 
184:   if ((flags & ~(uint16_t)VP_RECORD_FLAG_OPEN) != 0)
185:     {
186:       return -EBADMSG;
187:     }
188: 
189:   if (ssid_len == 0 || ssid_len > VELASIGHT_PROV_SSID_MAX)
190:     {
191:       return -EBADMSG;
192:     }
193: 
194:   if (psk_len != 0 &&
195:       (psk_len < VELASIGHT_PROV_PSK_MIN || psk_len > VELASIGHT_PROV_PSK_MAX))
196:     {
197:       return -EBADMSG;
198:     }
199: 
200:   if (((flags & VP_RECORD_FLAG_OPEN) != 0) != (psk_len == 0))
201:     {
202:       return -EBADMSG;
203:     }
204: 
205:   if (!vp_padding_is_zero(buf, VP_OFF_SSID, ssid_len,
206:                           VELASIGHT_PROV_SSID_MAX) ||
207:       !vp_padding_is_zero(buf, VP_OFF_PSK, psk_len,
208:                           VELASIGHT_PROV_PSK_MAX))
209:     {
210:       return -EBADMSG;
211:     }
212: 
213:   memset(&parsed, 0, sizeof(parsed));
214:   memcpy(parsed.ssid, buf + VP_OFF_SSID, ssid_len);
215:   memcpy(parsed.password, buf + VP_OFF_PSK, psk_len);
216:   parsed.generation   = vp_get32(buf + VP_OFF_GEN);
217:   parsed.open_network = psk_len == 0;
218: 
219:   /* The record can be structurally perfect and still describe credentials the
220:    * running code would refuse, for instance after a limit changes.  Treat that
221:    * as corrupt rather than handing the caller something it cannot use.
222:    */
223: 
224:   if (vp_credentials_validate(&parsed) < 0)
225:     {
226:       return -EBADMSG;
227:     }
228: 
229:   *cred = parsed;
230:   return 0;
231: }
232: 
233: static int vp_make_parent(const char *path)
234: {
235:   char dir[VP_STORE_PATH_MAX];
236:   const char *slash;
237:   size_t len;
238: 
239:   slash = strrchr(path, '/');
240:   if (slash == NULL || slash == path)
241:     {
242:       return 0;
243:     }
244: 
245:   len = (size_t)(slash - path);
246:   if (len >= sizeof(dir))
247:     {
248:       return -ENAMETOOLONG;
249:     }
250: 
251:   memcpy(dir, path, len);
252:   dir[len] = '\0';
253: 
254:   if (mkdir(dir, 0777) == 0 || errno == EEXIST)
255:     {
256:       return 0;
257:     }
258: 
259:   return -errno;
260: }
261: 
262: int vp_store_temp_path(const char *path, char *buf, size_t buflen)
263: {
264:   static const char name[] = "vpsave.tmp";
265:   const char *slash;
266:   size_t dirlen;
267: 
268:   if (path == NULL || buf == NULL)
269:     {
270:       return -EINVAL;
271:     }
272: 
273:   slash = strrchr(path, '/');
274:   dirlen = slash != NULL ? (size_t)(slash - path) + 1 : 0;
275: 
276:   if (dirlen + sizeof(name) > buflen)
277:     {
278:       return -E2BIG;
279:     }
280: 
281:   memcpy(buf, path, dirlen);
282:   memcpy(buf + dirlen, name, sizeof(name));
283:   return 0;
284: }
285: 
286: int vp_store_save(const char *path,
287:                   const struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred)
288: {
289:   uint8_t record[VP_RECORD_SIZE];
290:   char tmp[VP_STORE_PATH_MAX + 16];
291:   FILE *stream;
292:   int ret;
293: 
294:   if (path == NULL || cred == NULL)
295:     {
296:       return -EINVAL;
297:     }
298: 
299:   if (strlen(path) >= VP_STORE_PATH_MAX)
300:     {
301:       return -ENAMETOOLONG;
302:     }
303: 
304:   ret = vp_record_encode(record, sizeof(record), cred);
305:   if (ret < 0)
306:     {
307:       return ret;
308:     }
309: 
310:   ret = vp_make_parent(path);
311:   if (ret < 0)
312:     {
313:       return ret;
314:     }
315: 
316:   ret = vp_store_temp_path(path, tmp, sizeof(tmp));
317:   if (ret < 0)
318:     {
319:       return ret;
320:     }
321: 
322:   stream = fopen(tmp, "wb");
323:   if (stream == NULL)
324:     {
325:       return -errno;
326:     }
327: 
328:   /* Write, flush, fsync, close, rename.  Without the fsync the rename can be
329:    * durable while the data behind it is not, which on a power cut leaves a
330:    * record that passes its own CRC check by accident or fails it for no
331:    * reason the next boot can explain.
332:    */
333: 
334:   if (fwrite(record, 1, sizeof(record), stream) != sizeof(record) ||
335:       fflush(stream) != 0 || fsync(fileno(stream)) != 0)
336:     {
337:       ret = errno != 0 ? -errno : -EIO;
338:       fclose(stream);
339:       unlink(tmp);
340:       return ret;
341:     }
342: 
343:   if (fclose(stream) != 0)
344:     {
345:       ret = errno != 0 ? -errno : -EIO;
346:       unlink(tmp);
347:       return ret;
348:     }
349: 
350:   if (rename(tmp, path) < 0)
351:     {
352:       ret = -errno;
353:       unlink(tmp);
354:       return ret;
355:     }
356: 
357:   sync();
358:   return 0;
359: }
360: 
361: int vp_store_load(const char *path,
362:                   struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred)
363: {
364:   uint8_t record[VP_RECORD_SIZE + 1];
365:   FILE *stream;
366:   size_t nread;
367: 
368:   if (path == NULL || cred == NULL)
369:     {
370:       return -EINVAL;
371:     }
372: 
373:   stream = fopen(path, "rb");
374:   if (stream == NULL)
375:     {
376:       /* ENOTDIR belongs with ENOENT here: a directory component that is
377:        * missing, or is a file, means nothing was ever stored.  NuttX's FAT
378:        * reports ENOTDIR for the missing-directory case where Linux reports
379:        * ENOENT, and a device that has simply never been provisioned should
380:        * not look like a broken one.  EINVAL is deliberately left alone: on
381:        * that filesystem it means the configured path cannot be represented,
382:        * which is a misconfiguration worth seeing.
383:        */
384: 
385:       if (errno == ENOENT || errno == ENOTDIR)
386:         {
387:           return -ENOENT;
388:         }
389: 
390:       return -errno;
391:     }
392: 
393:   nread = fread(record, 1, sizeof(record), stream);
394:   fclose(stream);
395: 
396:   return vp_record_decode(record, nread, cred);
397: }
398: 
399: uint32_t vp_store_next_generation(const char *path)
400: {
401:   struct velasight_prov_credentials_s cred;
402: 
403:   if (vp_store_load(path, &cred) < 0 || cred.generation == UINT32_MAX)
404:     {
405:       return 1;
406:     }
407: 
408:   return cred.generation + 1;
409: }

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * app/provisioning_web/vp_store.h
3:  *
4:  * The persisted record and its atomic replacement.  Fixed size, versioned,
5:  * length-checked and CRC-protected, because a half-written credential file on
6:  * a VFAT volume that loses power mid-write is otherwise indistinguishable
7:  * from a valid one.
8:  *
9:  * The passphrase is stored in the clear.  VFAT has no permission model worth
10:  * relying on and this chip has no confirmed device key, so pretending to
11:  * encrypt would only hide the exposure.  What is controlled instead: it is
12:  * never logged, never echoed back over HTTP, and only read through the public
13:  * API.  Physical access to the SD-NAND reveals it.
14:  *
15:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
16:  ****************************************************************************/
17: 
18: #ifndef __APP_PROVISIONING_WEB_VP_STORE_H
19: #define __APP_PROVISIONING_WEB_VP_STORE_H
20: 
21: #include <stddef.h>
22: #include <stdint.h>
23: 
24: #include "velasight_provisioning.h"
25: 
26: /* Layout, little-endian:
27:  *
28:  *   0   4   magic "VSWP"
29:  *   4   2   version, currently 1
30:  *   6   2   flags, bit0 = open network
31:  *   8   4   generation
32:  *   12  1   ssid_len, 1..32
33:  *   13  1   psk_len, 0 or 8..63
34:  *   14  32  ssid, zero padded
35:  *   46  63  password, zero padded
36:  *   109 1   reserved, must be zero
37:  *   110 4   CRC32 of bytes 0..109
38:  */
39: 
40: #define VP_RECORD_SIZE    114
41: #define VP_RECORD_VERSION 1
42: #define VP_RECORD_MAGIC   "VSWP"
43: 
44: #define VP_RECORD_FLAG_OPEN 0x0001u
45: 
46: uint32_t vp_crc32(const void *data, size_t len);
47: 
48: /****************************************************************************
49:  * Name: vp_record_encode / vp_record_decode
50:  *
51:  * Description:
52:  *   Serialize and parse the record.  encode returns VP_RECORD_SIZE, -EINVAL
53:  *   for credentials that do not validate, or -E2BIG for a short buffer.
54:  *   decode returns 0 or -EBADMSG; it checks the magic, the version, both
55:  *   lengths, that the open flag agrees with psk_len, the reserved byte and
56:  *   the CRC.  A record that fails any of those is corrupt, not repairable.
57:  *
58:  ****************************************************************************/
59: 
60: int vp_record_encode(uint8_t *buf, size_t buflen,
61:                      const struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred);
62: 
63: int vp_record_decode(const uint8_t *buf, size_t len,
64:                      struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred);
65: 
66: /****************************************************************************
67:  * Name: vp_store_temp_path
68:  *
69:  * Description:
70:  *   The scratch file used by vp_store_save(), placed beside the record.
71:  *
72:  *   It is a fixed name rather than "<path>.tmp" because the SD-NAND is VFAT
73:  *   without long-name support: "wifi.bin.tmp" has two dots and every
74:  *   component must fit 8.3, so the obvious derivation is rejected with
75:  *   -EINVAL by the filesystem.  One save runs at a time, so a fixed name
76:  *   costs nothing.
77:  *
78:  *   Returns 0, or -E2BIG when the buffer is too small.
79:  *
80:  ****************************************************************************/
81: 
82: int vp_store_temp_path(const char *path, char *buf, size_t buflen);
83: 
84: /****************************************************************************
85:  * Name: vp_store_save
86:  *
87:  * Description:
88:  *   Write the record to the scratch file, flush it, fsync it, then rename it
89:  *   over the target, so a reader sees a complete record rather than a
90:  *   half-written one.  Creates the parent directory when it is missing.  On
91:  *   failure the scratch file is removed and any previous record is left
92:  *   intact.  Returns 0 or a negative errno.
93:  *
94:  *   On VFAT the rename is not a single atomic step -- NuttX's VFS unlinks an
95:  *   existing target first, and FAT's own rename refuses to overwrite -- so
96:  *   there is a brief window in which the record is absent.  That is the
97:  *   strongest guarantee this filesystem offers; a reader in that window gets
98:  *   -ENOENT, never a truncated record, because the CRC would catch it.
99:  *
100:  ****************************************************************************/
101: 
102: int vp_store_save(const char *path,
103:                   const struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred);
104: 
105: /****************************************************************************
106:  * Name: vp_store_load
107:  *
108:  * Description:
109:  *   Read and validate the record.  Returns 0, -ENOENT, -EBADMSG for a corrupt
110:  *   or wrong-sized file, or a negative errno.
111:  *
112:  ****************************************************************************/
113: 
114: int vp_store_load(const char *path,
115:                   struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred);
116: 
117: /****************************************************************************
118:  * Name: vp_store_next_generation
119:  *
120:  * Description:
121:  *   The generation to stamp on the next save: one past whatever is stored, or
122:  *   1 when nothing readable is there.  A corrupt record does not reset the
123:  *   counter to a value already used, it simply starts over at 1, which is the
124:  *   only honest answer when the old value is unreadable.
125:  *
126:  ****************************************************************************/
127: 
128: uint32_t vp_store_next_generation(const char *path);
129: 
130: #endif /* __APP_PROVISIONING_WEB_VP_STORE_H */

1: #
2: # For a description of the syntax of this configuration file,
3: # see the file kconfig-language.txt in the NuttX tools repository.
4: #
5: 
6: config LVX_USE_DEMO_CONTEST2026_264_PROVISION_WEB
7: 	bool "AP-mode provisioning web entry"
8: 	default n
9: 	depends on NET_TCP && NET_TCPBACKLOG
10: 	---help---
11: 		A minimal HTTP server that serves one form, accepts an SSID and a
12: 		passphrase, and writes them to persistent storage.  Meant to be
13: 		started by the application through
14: 		velasight_provisioning_start() once the radio is already in
15: 		SoftAP; it never changes the Wi-Fi role itself, so the
16: 		application stays in control of when the network may drop.
17: 
18: 		NET_TCPBACKLOG is required, not merely nice to have.  Without it
19: 		NuttX reports no poll event for a pending connection on a
20: 		listening socket (TCP_BACKLOG is the only source of POLLIN
21: 		there), and accept() blocks with no timeout, so a listener that
22: 		can still be stopped is impossible.  The observed symptom of
23: 		building without it is a service that reports "listening" and
24: 		then never answers a request.
25: 
26: 		The provision_web command is the manual front end for bringing
27: 		it up over the console.
28: 
29: 		The page is plain HTTP with no authentication, which is the usual
30: 		trade-off for a provisioning page on an access point.  Run it
31: 		only while provisioning.
32: 
33: if LVX_USE_DEMO_CONTEST2026_264_PROVISION_WEB
34: 
35: config VELASIGHT_PROVISION_STORE
36: 	string "Provisioning record path"
37: 	default "/mnt/sdnand/prov/wifi.bin"
38: 	---help---
39: 		Where the credential record is written.  The default is on
40: 		SD-NAND because that is the only persistent filesystem: /mnt is
41: 		pseudo-filesystem and /mnt/ram is a PSRAM ramdisk.  The parent
42: 		directory is created on demand.
43: 
44: 		Every path component must fit 8.3.  That SD-NAND is VFAT without
45: 		long-name support (CONFIG_FAT_LFN is not set), which rejects a
46: 		"velasight" directory or a "wifi-provision.bin" file with
47: 		-EINVAL rather than shortening it.
48: 
49: 		The passphrase is stored in the clear: VFAT has no permission
50: 		model to rely on and this part has no confirmed device key.  It
51: 		is never logged and never echoed back over HTTP, but physical
52: 		access to the SD-NAND reveals it.
53: 
54: config VELASIGHT_PROVISION_PORT

30: # NUTTX_USER_LIBRARIES: user-space defined libraries
31: # NUTTX_APPS_LIBRARIES: used for application linking typically added via `nuttx_add_application`
32: # NUTTX_EXTRA_LIBRARIES: additional external static libraries such as `libgcc,libm`
33: #
34: # In FLAT mode: all libraries are linked together.
35: # In PROTECTED mode: `NUTTX_KERNEL_LIBRARIES` and `NUTTX_EXTRA_LIBRARIES` link the kernel blob.
36: #                    `NUTTX_SYSTEM_LIBRARIES`,`NUTTX_USER_LIBRARIES` and `NUTTX_APPS_LIBRARIES` link user blob.
37: # In KERNEL mode: `NUTTX_KERNEL_LIBRARIES` and `NUTTX_EXTRA_LIBRARIES` link the kernel blob.
38: #                 link `NUTTX_APPS_LIBRARIES` to separate ELF file with 'NUTTX_SYSTEM_LIBRARIES' and 'NUTTX_USER_LIBRARIES'.
39: #
40: # The linking order follows these principles:
41: # `NUTTX_APPS_LIBRARIES` before `NUTTX_USER_LIBRARIES` befor `NUTTX_SYSTEM_LIBRARIES` befor `NUTTX_KERNEL_LIBRARIES`
42: # `NUTTX_EXTRA_LIBRARIES` at the very last
43: # ~~~
44: 
45: # Internal utility function
46: #
47: # Used by functions below, not to be used directly
48: 
49: function(nuttx_add_library_internal target)
50:   # ensure nuttx_context is created before this
51:   add_dependencies(${target} nuttx_context)
52: 
53:   # add specified search directories for CXX targets
54:   target_include_directories(
55:     ${target}
56:     PRIVATE
57:       $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:$<GENEX_EVAL:$<TARGET_PROPERTY:nuttx,NUTTX_CXX_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES>>>
58:   )
59: 
60:   # add main include directories
61:   target_include_directories(
62:     ${target} SYSTEM PRIVATE ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/include
63:                              ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/include)
64: 
65:   # Set global compile options & definitions We use the "nuttx" target to hold
66:   # these properties so that libraries added after this property is set can read
67:   # the final value at build time. The GENEX_EVAL allows the property to hold
68:   # generator expression itself
69:   target_compile_options(
70:     ${target}
71:     PRIVATE $<GENEX_EVAL:$<TARGET_PROPERTY:nuttx,NUTTX_COMPILE_OPTIONS>>)
72:   target_compile_definitions(
73:     ${target} PRIVATE $<GENEX_EVAL:$<TARGET_PROPERTY:nuttx,NUTTX_DEFINITIONS>>)
74:   target_include_directories(
75:     ${target}
76:     PRIVATE $<GENEX_EVAL:$<TARGET_PROPERTY:nuttx,NUTTX_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES>>)
77: 
78:   # Set install config for all library
79:   install(TARGETS ${target})
80:   # Set target information for debug and dump
81:   set_property(
82:     TARGET nuttx_target_interface
83:     APPEND
84:     PROPERTY ALL_TARGETS ${target})
85:   file(APPEND ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/targets "${target}\n")
86: endfunction()
87: 
88: # Auxiliary libraries
89: #
90: # The whole purpose of this is to overcome the limitation of CMake 3.16 to set
91: # source file properties from directories different from the one defining the
92: # target where the source file is used. This auxiliary library acts as an
93: # intermediate target that is usually linked to the system/kernel library
94: # defined at a higher level.
95: 
96: function(nuttx_add_aux_library target)
97:   # declare target
98:   add_library(${target} OBJECT ${ARGN})
99:   # make sure context and post time ordering
100:   add_dependencies(${target} apps_context)
101:   nuttx_add_library_internal(${target} ${ARGN})
102: endfunction()
103: 
104: # User (application) libraries
105: #
106: # An user library is a target which is defined as a collection of object files
107: # which is ultimately archived into the apps library
108: 
109: function(nuttx_add_user_library target)
110:   # declare target
111:   add_library(${target} OBJECT ${ARGN})
112:   # make sure context and post time ordering
113:   add_dependencies(${target} apps_context)
114:   add_dependencies(apps_post ${target})
115: 
116:   nuttx_add_library_internal(${target} ${ARGN})
117: 
118:   # link to final libapps
119:   target_link_libraries(apps PRIVATE ${target})
120: 
121:   # add apps/include to include path
122:   target_include_directories(${target} PRIVATE ${NUTTX_APPS_DIR}/include)
123: endfunction()
124: 
125: # System Libraries
126: #
127: # A system library is a library which is built into the OS but does not receive
128: # kernel-level flags (such as __KERNEL__). This is will be part of the userspace
129: # blob in kernel builds
130: 
131: function(nuttx_add_system_library target)
132:   # declare target
133:   add_library(${target} ${ARGN})
134:   # make sure context and post time ordering
135:   add_dependencies(${target} apps_context)
136:   add_dependencies(apps_post ${target})
137: 
138:   # add library to build
139:   nuttx_add_library_internal(${target} ${ARGN})
140: 
141:   # add to list of libraries to link to final nuttx binary
142:   set_property(GLOBAL APPEND PROPERTY NUTTX_SYSTEM_LIBRARIES ${target})
143: 
144:   set_property(
145:     TARGET nuttx_global
146:     APPEND
147:     PROPERTY NUTTX_ELF_LINK_LIBRARIES $<TARGET_FILE:${target}>)
148: 
149: endfunction()
150: 
151: # Kernel Libraries
152: #
153: # nuttx_add_kernel_library(target [SPLIT] [SAME_SOURCES] [sources ...])
154: #
155: # For non-kernel builds, this defines an OS library which will receive
156: # kernel-level flags (such as __KERNEL__) and will be linked into nuttx binary
157: # For kernel builds, the same happens unless SPLIT is specified. In this case
158: # both a <target> and a k<target> library will be defined, but only the latter
159: # having the kernel-level flags. In this case, both libraries will receive the
160: # same set of sources (the original <target> should be used by the user to add
161: # sources).
162: 
163: function(nuttx_add_kernel_library target)
164:   cmake_parse_arguments(ARGS SPLIT "" "" ${ARGN})
165:   set(SRCS ${ARGS_UNPARSED_ARGUMENTS})
166: 
167:   if(ARGS_SPLIT AND NOT CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT)
168:     set(kernel_target k${target})
169: 
170:     # add non-kernel (system) library
171:     nuttx_add_system_library(${target} ${SRCS})
172:   else()
173:     set(kernel_target ${target})
174:   endif()
175: 
176:   # add kernel library
177:   add_library(${kernel_target} ${SRCS})
178:   nuttx_add_library_internal(${kernel_target} ${SRCS})
179:   set_property(GLOBAL APPEND PROPERTY NUTTX_KERNEL_LIBRARIES ${kernel_target})
180: 
181:   # Add kernel options & definitions See note above in
182:   # nuttx_add_library_internal() on syntax and nuttx target use
183:   if(NOT ARGS_SPLIT OR NOT "${target}" STREQUAL "${kernel_target}")
184:     target_compile_options(
185:       ${kernel_target}
186:       PRIVATE
187:         $<GENEX_EVAL:$<TARGET_PROPERTY:nuttx,NUTTX_KERNEL_COMPILE_OPTIONS>>)
188:     target_compile_definitions(
189:       ${kernel_target}
190:       PRIVATE $<GENEX_EVAL:$<TARGET_PROPERTY:nuttx,NUTTX_KERNEL_DEFINITIONS>>)
191:     target_include_directories(
192:       ${kernel_target}
193:       PRIVATE
194:         $<GENEX_EVAL:$<TARGET_PROPERTY:nuttx,NUTTX_KERNEL_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES>>)
195:   endif()
196: 
197:   if(NOT "${target}" STREQUAL "${kernel_target}")
198:     # The k${target} lib will have the same sources added to that ${target} lib.
199:     # This allows to do target_sources(${target} ..) easily
200:     target_sources(${kernel_target}
201:                    PRIVATE $<TARGET_PROPERTY:${target},SOURCES>)
202: 
203:     # same for include directories
204:     target_include_directories(
205:       ${kernel_target} PRIVATE $<TARGET_PROPERTY:${target},INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES>)
206:   endif()
207: endfunction()
208: 
209: include(nuttx_parse_function_args)
210: 
211: define_property(
212:   GLOBAL
213:   PROPERTY NUTTX_LIBRARIES
214:   BRIEF_DOCS "NuttX libs"
215:   FULL_DOCS "List of all NuttX libraries")
216: 
217: # =============================================================================
218: #
219: # nuttx_add_library
220: #
221: # Wrapper of cmake add_library but with nuttx platform dependencies
222: #
223: function(nuttx_add_library target)
224:   add_library(${target} ${ARGN})
225:   # make sure context and post time ordering
226:   add_dependencies(${target} apps_context)
227:   add_dependencies(apps_post ${target})
228:   set_property(GLOBAL APPEND PROPERTY NUTTX_USER_LIBRARIES ${target})
229: 
230:   set_property(
231:     TARGET nuttx_global
232:     APPEND
233:     PROPERTY NUTTX_ELF_LINK_LIBRARIES $<TARGET_FILE:${target}>)
234: 
235:   # Set apps global compile options & definitions hold by nuttx_apps_interface
236:   target_compile_options(
237:     ${target}
238:     PRIVATE
239:       $<GENEX_EVAL:$<TARGET_PROPERTY:nuttx_apps_interface,APPS_COMPILE_OPTIONS>>
240:   )
241:   target_compile_definitions(
242:     ${target}
243:     PRIVATE
244:       $<GENEX_EVAL:$<TARGET_PROPERTY:nuttx_apps_interface,APPS_COMPILE_DEFINITIONS>>
245:   )
246:   target_include_directories(
247:     ${target}
248:     PRIVATE
249:       $<GENEX_EVAL:$<TARGET_PROPERTY:nuttx_apps_interface,APPS_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES>>
250:   )
251:   nuttx_add_library_internal(${target})
252: endfunction()
253: 
254: # =============================================================================
255: #
256: # nuttx_add_extra_library
257: #
258: # Add extra library to extra attribute, extra library will be treated as an
259: # import target and have a complete full path this will be used to avoid adding
260: # the -l prefix to the link target between different cmake versions and
261: # platformss
262: #
263: function(nuttx_add_extra_library)
264:   foreach(extra_lib ${ARGN})
265:     # define the target name of the extra library
266:     string(REGEX REPLACE "[^a-zA-Z0-9]" "_" extra_target "${extra_lib}")
267:     # set the absolute path of the library for the import target
268:     if(NOT TARGET ${extra_target})
269:       nuttx_library_import(${extra_target} ${extra_lib})
270:       set_property(GLOBAL APPEND PROPERTY NUTTX_EXTRA_LIBRARIES ${extra_target})
271:       if(CONFIG_BUILD_PROTECTED)
272:         set_property(GLOBAL APPEND PROPERTY NUTTX_USER_EXTRA_LIBRARIES
273:                                             ${extra_target})
274:       endif()
275:       set_property(
276:         TARGET nuttx_global
277:         APPEND
278:         PROPERTY NUTTX_ELF_LINK_EXTRA_LIBRARIES $<TARGET_FILE:${extra_target}>)
279:     endif()
280:   endforeach()

362:        OR CONFIG_BUILD_KERNEL

369:         ${MODULE}

372:         SRCS

374:         PRIORITY

401:       add_library(${TARGET} ${SRCS})
402: 
403:       nuttx_add_library_internal(${TARGET})
404:       # add to list of application libraries
405: 
406:       set_property(GLOBAL APPEND PROPERTY NUTTX_APPS_LIBRARIES ${TARGET})
407: 
408:       if(NOT NO_MAIN_ALIAS)
409:         # provide main() alias
410:         list(GET SRCS 0 MAIN_SRC)
411:         set_property(
412:           SOURCE ${MAIN_SRC}
413:           APPEND
414:           PROPERTY COMPILE_DEFINITIONS main=${NAME}_main)
415:       endif()
416:     endif()
417: 
418:   else()

420:     add_custom_target(${TARGET})

437:   else()

441:

444:   else()
445:     set_target_properties(${TARGET} PROPERTIES APP_STACK
446:                                                ${CONFIG_DEFAULT_TASK_STACKSIZE})
447:   endif()

44: # ~~~
45: # Allow external toolchain to provide custom nuttx_add_elf_app implementation
46: #
47: # External toolchains can define their own nuttx_add_elf_app by:
48: # 1. Defining the function before this file is included
49: # 2. The custom function MUST set RESULT_TARGET variable in parent scope
50: #
51: # Example in toolchain file:
52: #   function(nuttx_add_elf_app)
53: #     # ...  parse arguments
54: #     # ...  custom implementation
55: #     set(RESULT_TARGET "custom_target_name" PARENT_SCOPE)

60: if(NOT COMMAND nuttx_add_elf_app)
61:   # ~~~
62:   # nuttx_add_elf_app
63:   #
64:   # Description:
65:   #   Creates a standalone executable application (loadable module, kernel ELF,
66:   #   or dynamic library) as opposed to a static library.
67:   #
68:   #   This function can be overridden by external toolchains to provide custom
69:   #   ELF building behavior.
70:   #
71:   # Usage:
72:   #   nuttx_add_elf_app(
73:   #     NAME <string>
74:   #     MODULE <string>
75:   #     DYNLIB <string>
76:   #     SRCS <list>
77:   #     [ PRIORITY <string> ]
78:   #     [ STACKSIZE <string> ]
79:   #     [ HEAPSIZE <string> ]
80:   #     [ UID <string> ]
81:   #     [ GID <string> ]
82:   #     [ MODE <string> ]
83:   #     [ COMPILE_FLAGS <list> ]
84:   #     [ LINK_FLAGS <list> ]
85:   #     [ INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES <list> ]
86:   #     [ DEPENDS <list> ]
87:   #     [ DEFINITIONS <list> ])
88:   #
89:   # Parameters:
90:   #   NAME       : name of the application
91:   #   MODULE     : module configuration ("m" for loadable)
92:   #   DYNLIB     : dynamic library flag ("y" for dynlib)
93:   #   SRCS       : source files
94:   #   Other parameters: same as nuttx_add_application
95:   #
96:   # Returns:
97:   #   Sets RESULT_TARGET variable in parent scope
98:   # ~~~
99: 
100:   function(nuttx_add_elf_app)
101:     nuttx_parse_function_args(
102:       FUNC
103:       nuttx_add_elf_app
104:       ONE_VALUE
105:       NAME
106:       PRIORITY
107:       STACKSIZE
108:       UID
109:       GID
110:       MODE
111:       HEAPSIZE
112:       MODULE
113:       DYNLIB
114:       MULTI_VALUE
115:       COMPILE_FLAGS
116:       LINK_FLAGS
117:       INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES
118:       SRCS
119:       DEPENDS
120:       DEFINITIONS
121:       OPTIONS
122:       ARGN
123:       ${ARGN})
124: 
125:     # create as standalone executable (loadable application or "module")
126:     set(ELF_TARGET "${NAME}")
127: 
128:     # determine the compiled elf mode
129:     if(CONFIG_BUILD_KERNEL)
130:       set(KERNEL_ELF_MODE True) # kernel elf will link all user libs
131:     elseif("${MODULE}" STREQUAL "m")
132:       set(LOADABLE_ELF_MODE True) # loadable elf only link extra libs
133:     elseif("${DYNLIB}" STREQUAL "y")
134:       set(DYNLIB_ELF_MODE True) # dynlib elf dont need start obj and other lib
135:     endif()
136: 
137:     # Use ELF capable toolchain, by building manually and overwriting the
138:     # non-elf output
139:     if(NOT CMAKE_C_ELF_COMPILER)
140:       set(ELF_NAME "${NAME}")
141:       set(ELF_TARGET "ELF_${NAME}")
142:       add_library(${ELF_TARGET} ${SRCS})
143:       add_dependencies(${ELF_TARGET} apps_post)
144:       if(TARGET STARTUP_OBJS)
145:         add_dependencies(${ELF_TARGET} STARTUP_OBJS)
146:       endif()
147:       if(NOT "${CMAKE_C_COMPILER}" MATCHES "gcc$|clang$")
148:         set(USE_LINKER True)
149:       endif()
150:       if(STACKSIZE)
151:         set(SYMBOL_STACKSIZE --add-symbol nx_stacksize=${STACKSIZE})
152:       endif()
153:       if(PRIORITY)
154:         if(PRIORITY STREQUAL "SCHED_PRIORITY_DEFAULT")
155:           set(PRIORITY "0")
156:         endif()
157:         set(SYMBOL_PRIORITY --add-symbol nx_priority=${PRIORITY})
158:       endif()
159:       if(CONFIG_SCHED_USER_IDENTITY)

89: /****************************************************************************
90:  * A blunt HTTP client: send a request, read until the peer closes.  The close
91:  * matters -- the service must not leave the connection open after answering,
92:  * because the application is about to take the network away.
93:  ****************************************************************************/
94: 
95: static int http_exchange(const char *request, char *reply, size_t replylen)
96: {
97:   struct sockaddr_in addr;
98:   struct timeval tv;
99:   size_t total = 0;
100:   int fd;
101: 
102:   fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
103:   if (fd < 0)
104:     {
105:       return -errno;
106:     }
107: 
108:   tv.tv_sec  = 5;
109:   tv.tv_usec = 0;
110:   setsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_RCVTIMEO, &tv, sizeof(tv));
111:   setsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_SNDTIMEO, &tv, sizeof(tv));
112: 
113:   memset(&addr, 0, sizeof(addr));
114:   addr.sin_family = AF_INET;
115:   addr.sin_port   = htons(g_port);
116:   addr.sin_addr.s_addr = htonl(INADDR_LOOPBACK);
117: 
118:   if (connect(fd, (struct sockaddr *)&addr, sizeof(addr)) < 0)
119:     {
120:       int error = -errno;
121:       close(fd);
122:       return error;
123:     }
124: 
125:   if (write(fd, request, strlen(request)) < 0)
126:     {
127:       int error = -errno;
128:       close(fd);
129:       return error;
130:     }
131: 
132:   for (; ; )
133:     {
134:       ssize_t n = read(fd, reply + total, replylen - 1 - total);
135: 
136:       if (n < 0)
137:         {
138:           int error = -errno;
139:           close(fd);
140:           return error;
141:         }
142: 
143:       if (n == 0)
144:         {
145:           break;
146:         }
147: 
148:       total += (size_t)n;
149:       if (total >= replylen - 1)
150:         {
151:           break;
152:         }
153:     }
154: 
155:   close(fd);
156:   reply[total] = '\0';
157:   return (int)total;
158: }

172:           return 0;
173:         }
174: 
175:       g_port = (uint16_t)(g_port + 1);
176:     }
177: 
178:   return ret;

1: # AP 模式简易配网 Web
2: 
3: 板子进入 SoftAP 后调用一个入口，手机连上热点打开网页填 SSID 和密码，凭据原子写入
4: SD-NAND，应用通过回调知道「第 N 次保存成功」。
5: 
6: **本服务不切换 Wi-Fi 模式。** 不调用 `wapi`、不 `ifup/ifdown`、不关联、不启停 DHCPD。
7: 进 SoftAP 和切回 STA 全部由应用或人工完成——只有应用知道什么时候可以让网络断开。
8: 
9: ## 应用侧用法
10: 
11: ```c
12: #include "velasight_provisioning.h"
13: 
14: static void on_saved(int status, uint32_t generation, void *arg)
15: {
16:   if (status < 0)
17:     {
18:       /* 写盘失败，凭据没存下来 */
19:       return;
20:     }
21: 
22:   /* 页面已经发完、连接已经关闭，这里可以安全地切回 STA */
23:   struct velasight_prov_credentials_s cred;
24: 
25:   if (velasight_provisioning_load(&cred) == 0)
26:     {
27:       /* cred.ssid / cred.password / cred.open_network */
28:       velasight_provisioning_stop();   /* 从回调里调用是安全的 */
29:       /* 这里做你自己的 STA 切换与关联 */
30:     }
31: }
32: 
33: struct velasight_prov_config_s cfg =
34: {
35:   .port       = 0,          /* 0 → 80 */
36:   .one_shot   = false,      /* true = 成功保存一次后自动停止 */
37:   .store_path = NULL,       /* NULL → CONFIG_VELASIGHT_PROVISION_STORE */
38:   .on_saved   = on_saved,
39:   .cb_arg     = NULL,
40: };
41: 
42: velasight_provisioning_start(&cfg);
43: ```
44: 
45: | 函数 | 说明 |
46: |---|---|
47: | `velasight_provisioning_start(cfg)` | 绑定端口并启动监听线程。已在运行返回 `-EALREADY`；`cfg` 可为 NULL 表示全默认 |
48: | `velasight_provisioning_stop()` | 关闭监听并回收线程。未运行返回 `-EALREADY`。可在回调里调用 |
49: | `velasight_provisioning_is_running()` | 是否在监听 |
50: | `velasight_provisioning_generation()` | 本次运行内成功保存的次数，未保存过为 0 |
51: | `velasight_provisioning_load(out)` | 读取凭据。`-ENOENT` 未配网，`-EBADMSG` 记录损坏 |
52: | `velasight_provisioning_load_from(path, out)` | 指定路径读取 |
53: 
54: 回调只带状态码和序号，不带凭据：要凭据请显式 `load()`，这样密码不会顺着每一个只想收
55: 通知的回调链路走一遍。回调固定在**响应发完并关闭连接之后**触发——反过来会在应用切走
56: Wi-Fi 时截断响应，手机上看到的是「提交失败」而实际已经存了。
57: 
58: 监听线程是 pthread，pthread 不会比创建它的任务活得更久，所以应用要在自己的长驻任务里
59: 调 `start()`。
60: 
61: ## 手工上板验证
62: 
63: 先切 SoftAP（详见 `docs/WiFi使用说明.md`）：
64: 
65: ```sh
66: ifdown wlan0
67: ifup wlan0
68: wapi mode wlan0 3
69: wapi freq wlan0 6 1
70: wapi psk wlan0 <8-63字节密码> 3
71: wapi essid wlan0 VelaSight_AP 1
72: dhcpd_start wlan0            # 板子成为 192.168.10.1
73: ```
74: 
75: 再起配网页面：
76: 
77: ```sh
78: provision_web run            # 前台运行，Ctrl-C 停止
79: provision_web run 8080       # 换端口
80: provision_web run --one-shot # 成功保存一次后返回
81: ```
82: 
83: 手机连上 `VelaSight_AP` 后浏览器打开 `http://192.168.10.1/`，填 SSID 和密码提交。
84: 
85: 查看已存内容（**不打印密码**）：
86: 
87: ```sh
88: provision_web show
89: # provision_web: ssid=AIPC security=wpa2 password=set generation=1
90: provision_web path
91: # /mnt/sdnand/prov/wifi.bin
92: ```
93: 
94: 没有手机或 Wi-Fi 客户端时，用板子自己的回环把整条链路走一遍（会用测试网络覆盖已存
95: 记录，不需要进 SoftAP）：
96: 
97: ```sh
98: provision_web selftest
99: # provision_web selftest: PASS, 14 checks, 0 failures
100: reboot
101: provision_web show      # 证明记录跨重启存活
102: ```
103: 
104: 验完切回 STA，仍然按 `docs/WiFi使用说明.md`：
105: 
106: ```sh
107: dhcpd_stop
108: ifdown wlan0
109: ifup wlan0
110: wapi mode wlan0 2
111: wapi psk wlan0 <路由器密码> 3
112: wapi essid wlan0 <2.4G_SSID> 1
113: renew wlan0
114: ```
115: 
116: ## HTTP 表面
117: 
118: | 请求 | 响应 |
119: |---|---|
120: | `GET /`、`GET /index.html` | 200 表单页 |
121: | `POST /save`（`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`） | 200 成功页 / 400 校验失败 / 500 写盘失败 |
122: | 其他方法 | 405 |
123: | 其他路径 | 404 |
124: | 缺 `Content-Length` | 411 |
125: | body > 512 字节 | 413 |
126: | 非表单 Content-Type | 415 |
127: | 请求头 > 2048 字节 | 431 |
128: | `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` | 400 |
129: 
130: 读超时 5 秒，一次只服务一个连接，每个连接答完即关闭。成功页只回显经过 HTML 转义的
131: SSID；**密码永不回显、永不进日志**。
132: 
133: 校验规则：SSID 1–32 字节且不含控制字符；密码留空表示开放网络，否则必须 8–63 字节的
134: 可打印 ASCII。表单缺 `ssid` 直接 400；`ssid` 或 `password` 重复出现按歧义拒绝，不猜。
135: 
136: ## NAND 记录
137: 
138: 默认 `/mnt/sdnand/prov/wifi.bin`，固定 114 字节，小端：
139: 
140: | 偏移 | 长度 | 字段 |
141: |---|---|---|
142: | 0 | 4 | 魔数 `VSWP` |
143: | 4 | 2 | 版本，当前 1 |
144: | 6 | 2 | 标志位，bit0 = 开放网络 |
145: | 8 | 4 | generation |
146: | 12 | 1 | ssid_len，1..32 |
147: | 13 | 1 | psk_len，0 或 8..63 |
148: | 14 | 32 | SSID，补零 |
149: | 46 | 63 | 密码，补零 |
150: | 109 | 1 | 保留，必须 0 |
151: | 110 | 4 | CRC32（IEEE，覆盖 0..109） |
152: 
153: 落盘顺序是同目录的 `vpsave.tmp` → `fflush` → `fsync` → `close` → `rename` → `sync()`。
154: 魔数、版本、两个长度、开放标志与 `psk_len` 的自洽性、补零区、保留字节和 CRC 逐项校验，
155: 任何一项不过按 `-EBADMSG` 处理，不做「尽力恢复」。
156: 
157: 只保留最新一份，提交即替换，generation 递增。凭据不镜像到 kvdb——需要的话由应用读出后
158: 自己写。
159: 
160: ## 三条平台约束（都是上板实测撞出来的）
161: 
162: 改动这三处之前先读这一节，否则会重现同样的故障：
163: 
164: 1. **`/mnt` 必须保持伪文件系统。** PSRAM ramdisk 挂在 `/mnt/ram`，不是 `/mnt`。
165:    NuttX 不允许在真实文件系统内部再挂载，`/mnt` 上挂了 littlefs 之后 SD-NAND 的
166:    `/mnt/sdnand` 会以 `-ENOTDIR` 挂载失败，持久存储静默消失。
167: 2. **`CONFIG_NET_TCPBACKLOG=y` 是必需项。** 没有它 listening socket 上不会有
168:    `POLLIN`，`accept()` 也无超时，可停止的监听线程无法实现；症状是打印了 listening
169:    之后什么都不回。本模块 Kconfig 已 `depends on` 它，配置错误会在编译期暴露。
170: 3. **SD-NAND 是不带长名的 VFAT。** `CONFIG_FAT_LFN` 未开，路径每一段必须符合 8.3。
171:    `velasight/`、`wifi-provision.bin` 都会被 `-EINVAL` 拒绝，把 `.tmp` 追加到
172:    `wifi.bin` 得到两个点也非法——所以临时文件是固定名 `vpsave.tmp`。主机测试会逐段
173:    校验默认路径的 8.3 合规性。
174: 
175: VFAT 上 `rename` 不是单步原子：NuttX 的 VFS 先 unlink 目标，FAT 的 `rename` 拒绝覆盖。
176: 所以存在「旧记录已删、新记录未就位」的极短窗口，此时读到 `-ENOENT`；读不到截断记录，
177: 因为长度和 CRC 都会拒绝。
178: 
179: ## 安全边界
180: 
181: - **服务是明文 HTTP 且无鉴权。** 热点覆盖内的任何设备都能提交。缓解手段：SoftAP 带
182:   WPA2 密码、只在配网期间开启、配完 `stop()`，或者用 `one_shot`。
183: - **密码在 NAND 上是明文。** VFAT 没有可信的权限模型，这颗芯片也没有已确认可用的设备
184:   密钥来源，所以不假装做静态加密。可控的部分是：不写日志、不回显、只走公共 API 读取。
185:   物理拿到 SD-NAND 就能读到密码。
186: - 不要把真实密码写进仓库、提交信息或测试日志。
187: 
188: ## 测试
189: 
190: ```sh
191: cd app/provisioning_web/tests && make        # 表单/记录/HTTP/服务器
192: cd app/web_tool/host/tests   && make         # 全量回归，已包含上面这一组
193: ```
194: 
195: `vp_form.c`、`vp_store.c`、`vp_http.c` 不含任何 NuttX 头文件，`vp_server.c` 只用 POSIX
196: socket，所以连 accept 循环、回调时序和 one-shot 都能在主机上跑完，剩给真板的只有
197: 「SoftAP 和 SD-NAND 是否真的在」。
198: 
199: ## 文件
200: 
201: | 文件 | 职责 |
202: |---|---|
203: | `include/velasight_provisioning.h` | 公共 API 与凭据结构 |
204: | `vp_form.c/.h` | URL 解码与字段校验 |
205: | `vp_store.c/.h` | 记录编解码、CRC32、原子落盘 |
206: | `vp_http.c/.h` | 请求解析、页面生成、HTML 转义 |
207: | `vp_server.c` | 监听线程、连接处理、生命周期与回调时序 |
208: | `provisioning_web_main.c` | `provision_web` 命令 |
209: 
210: 设计文档：`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-ap-provisioning-web-design.md`
